messages.author: 8c681cfdb03053cb
messages.subject: No observations on a transect
parts:
Hello again, 

Now that i understand what effort means i have a question about it regarding my dataset. 

I have 15 transect lines but on 2 of the lines i have not counted a pigeon. How to i place these 'no observation' data in my dataset?

Do i just put in effort and leave the distances blank or do i completely leave out the two transect lines and their effort?

with kind regards, 

Casolyn van der Schoot

messages.author: 75e0b0abcbafbc7d
messages.subject: Re: [distance-sampling] No observations on a transect
parts:
Casolyn

Under no circumstances should you remove transects (and effort) from your data if there are no detections on transects.  This will lead to gross over-estimates of abundance because the software will assume pigeons were detected on every transect you visited (because you removed transects when pigeons were not detected).

For transects without detections, you record everything about the transect, its label, the amount of effort, but for distance from transect, you set that value to "NA" if you are using the R package. If using Distance for Windows, leave the distance field blank when importing your data.

messages.subject: Re: [distance-sampling] No observations on a transect
parts:
Nehafta

If you install the Distance package from CRAN you will find lots of example data sets included in the package. Examining them will give you a good idea regarding the data structure you can implement in spreadsheet software for your data entry.

Basically it is a hierarchial data structure with the global data layer being the study area. The study area may be divided into strata. Within strata there are transects. Detections are associated with transects.

There is information about analysis of distance sampling data using R in Chapter 7 of our online workshop

https://workshops.distancesampling.org/online-course/syllabus/Chapter7/
Chapter 7 Analysis using R
Teaching distance sampling through video lectures and computer exercises.
workshops.distancesampling.org
